title: Superman: The Mechanical Monsters
studio: Fleischer Studios (dir. Dave Fleischer); Paramount Pictures
cut: 7:40-9:10 of the archive copy (90 s); deinterlaced (bwdif), 8 px of DVD edge crop, 624x472
contents: Climax: Clark sneaks into the inventor's lair, the army of numbered flying robots attacks Superman, he smashes them apart, and saves Lois from a bucket over molten metal as the lair burns.
pd_us: US: PD. All 17 Fleischer/Famous Superman shorts lapsed because the copyrights were not renewed (Wikipedia 'Superman (1940s cartoons)': 'All eventually fell into the public domain, due to National's failure to renew their copyrights'). Warner Bros./DC owns the original film elements, but not copyright in this public print.
pd_korea: Korea: PD. Korean Copyright Act Art. 42 protects cinematographic works for 70 years from publication (50 years before the 1 Jul 2013 amendment, which did not revive expired works); a film published in 1941 expired at the end of 2011 at the latest, so 1955-or-earlier films are PD. Korea's 1996 Berne restoration only covered foreign works still within the Korean term, so it does not apply.
trademark_caveat: SUPERMAN, the S-shield and the costume are DC Comics trademarks. Footage reuse is fine; don't name or brand the channel/thumbnails with Superman or the S-shield, or imply DC endorsement. Describe it as 'the 1941 Fleischer cartoon'.
underlying_work_caveat: The cartoon is based on the Superman comic (Action Comics #1, 1938, still in US copyright until 1 Jan 2034; in Korea the comic's term runs on the authors' lives). Under Russell v. Price (9th Cir. 1977) the copyright of an underlying work can still reach a PD film derivative. In practice these shorts are freely distributed (archive.org, budget DVDs) without enforcement, but it is the riskiest item here: use the clip as footage, don't build merchandise or new Superman stories from it.
audio: kept: original 1941 soundtrack (Sammy Timberg score), AAC 160k mono
